messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — noticed a growing backlog in billing ingest this morning, mostly around retry storms from a mobile SDK push. Queue depth on billing-ingest increased ~3x.
mira: saw that on the dashboard too. any particular customer or region?
alex: concentrated in eu-west, ~85% from one app id, a lot of duplicate retry traffic. looks like the client retries without exponential backoff.
sam: stack trace shows a timeout at the gateway layer, then client retries — we’re getting duplicate token-attribution events which are expensive to process.
jordan: painful. we should avoid dropping audit-critical events but also can't let pipeline OOM. Proposal: introduce short-term throttling at ingress with a header flag for priority and an "audit" pass-through lane.
alex: exactly. idea: X-Redwood-Priority: audit|standard|background
- audit => always store full raw event and route to audit-store + realtime accounting
- standard => usual path
- background => best-effort, sample/drop under pressure
mira: nice. how do we guarantee billing correctness if we drop "background"? finance would lose revenue visibility.
katie (finance): we can't drop events that map to billable tokens. any sampling must be restricted to telemetry or non-billable helper calls. If you can guarantee that background=non-billable, maybe ok.
sam: we can detect billable by payload.type and token_count > 0 at gateway before throttling. plan: gate by billable flag, never throttle billable events. only apply sampling to non-billable traces/logging/diagnostic calls.
jordan: tradeoff: extra logic at the gateway increases tail latency. alternative: enqueue everything but have a background worker that can drop low-priority events when backpressure hits. advantage: keep gateway simple.
alex: true. but enqueueing increases storage and S3 cost; we need a plan that minimizes downstream CPU cost too.
mira: another concern: attribution. Right now attribution resolution happens in enrichment stage — if we drop early, we might lose attribution keys required for audits.
sam: solution: materialize a small attribution token at gateway (hash of customer_id + request_id) and persist as part of the raw event header. That lets downstream dedupe/attribution without full enrichment.
alex: example header we could add:
```
X-Redwood-Attribution: cust_123|r:abc123|h:9f8a
X-Redwood-Priority: standard
```
mira: good. also we need to keep dedupe window boundaries. right now it's 24h; do we keep that or shorten temporarily?
jordan: keep 24h for safety. but we can add an eventual compaction job to reconcile duplicates older than 7 days for low-dollar accounts.
katie (finance): acceptable if reconciliation never changes invoice totals for >99.99% accounts. we need an audit trail for any changes.
sam: operational plan:
- roll gateway header change behind a feature flag
- add per-customer circuit breaker that raises priority for customers with SLA
- add background dropper for non-billable events when queue latency > 2s
- persist raw events in cold storage for 30 days (audit window) but only process standard events for realtime billing
alex: timeline?
mira: quick spike protection implemented in <24h (gateway flag + queue dropper), header + attribution materialization in 3 days, reconciliation job + compaction in 2 weeks.
jordan: sounds reasonable. I'll open a short RFC with tradeoffs and cost estimates.
alex: +1. quick note: make sure ingest-bot posts alerts when dropper kicks in and include sample keys so we can trace customer impact.
ingest-bot: alert configured: billing-ingest dropper fired — 1.2% of non-billable events dropped in last 5m. See /ops/ingest/drops/200345 for details :warning:
mira: Thanks — let's keep finance looped until header rollout.
katie (finance): will monitor. please tag me on the RFC. :thumbsup:
